body.title: Rewrite the S001 contract test that asserted StructuredRenderer is implemented nowhere
body.summary: S001 exported `StructuredRenderer<T>` and pinned, by test, that no file among docs-review-panel.ts / docs-review-client.ts / docs-sections.ts / markdown-style.ts annotates a value with it. That assertion was written to hold only until the first implementer arrived, and this Story is that implementer. REWRITE it, do not delete it: the type is still exported, it is implemented in exactly ONE place — the functional-requirements renderer — and the other listed files still declare none. The replacement must still fail if a renderer appears somewhere unsanctioned. Record it in the commit as a deliberate, scoped narrowing, the same kind S001 made to the no-innerHTML assertion, never an incidental relaxation.
acceptanceChecks: The rewritten test still asserts `export type StructuredRenderer<` is present in docs-review-panel.ts.
It asserts exactly one implementation site and names it; introducing a second annotation in an unlisted file must turn it red — proved by actually adding one, not by reading the assertion.
docs-review-client.ts, docs-sections.ts and markdown-style.ts are still asserted to declare none.
The test's name and its comment state that this is a deliberate narrowing at the first implementer, so a later reader cannot mistake it for an eroded invariant.

tests.name: t6 (contract): StructuredRenderer is still exported and now implemented in exactly ONE named place, with the other three files still declaring none
t6 (mutation): add a second StructuredRenderer annotation in an unlisted file -> the rewritten contract test fails
